alert.name: warden-dev-billing-db-free-storage
alert.summary: Free storage space of the billing database below 2 GiB

logs: ALARM AWS/RDS/FreeStorageSpace DBInstanceIdentifier=warden-dev-billing-db stat=Minimum period=300s threshold LessThanThreshold 2147483648.0 datapoints=1/1 missing=missing state=ALARM
CHANGE 2026-10-10T05:02:17Z rds.amazonaws.com ModifyDBInstance on warden-dev-billing-db by role/warden-dev-terraform

STATE rds_instance warden-dev-billing-db DBInstanceStatus=storage-full DBInstanceClass=db.t4g.medium Engine=postgres EngineVersion=16.4 MultiAZ=false AllocatedStorage=100 StorageType=gp3 Iops=3000 BackupRetentionPeriod=7 PendingModifiedValues=none CACertificateIdentifier=rds-ca-rsa2048-g1
context.alert_text: Free storage space of the billing database below 2 GiB

root_cause.hypothesis: The instance has hit storage-full because WAL/transaction logs are not being recycled, most likely due to a stalled or inactive logical replication slot retaining log segments at the same volume as the transaction logs themselves.
evidence: M6/M7 show transaction log usage and replication slot usage at nearly identical magnitude (~61GB), consistent with WAL retention by an unconsumed slot
M8 oldest replication slot lag is extremely high, matching the disk usage value, suggesting the slot has not advanced and is blocking WAL cleanup
ruled_out: High write IOPS/connections (M2, M4) are within normal dev-scale ranges and don't by themselves explain storage exhaustion
CPU/memory (M5, M10) are not abnormal, so this isn't a compute-driven incident

proposal.reasoning: The database is in storage-full state (C3) with free storage below the 2GiB alarm threshold (C1, M1). Immediate relief requires increasing allocated storage to restore write availability while the underlying replication-slot/WAL retention issue is investigated and resolved out-of-band (e.g., dropping a stale slot).
proposal.expected_effect: Increases AllocatedStorage on warden-dev-billing-db, moving FreeStorageSpace back above the alarm threshold and clearing the storage-full condition so writes can resume.

reasons: The proposal claims scale_up is irreversible; WARDEN's action table classifies it reversible. A human should reconcile that before anything runs.
none of the cited evidence bears on scale_up (it names none of: memory, oom, throttl, cpu, concurrency, pool...).
